note: Register of periodic processes in the guest (protocol v5, proposal 5.6). Nominal values from the source lines and from documented defaults; G2 measures the real periods from the guest journal. measured: the real spacings of an entry, before and after a change, each with the record it comes from (so far the autovacuum launcher, lead's answer to Q9). lab/tests/test_periods.py finds every Restart=, timer and waiting loop in the deployed files of lab/ and fails on one this register does not name at its line. A process-creating entry that is active is bounded or has a random delay. random_s: the range added to period_s.

periods.name: hyptcn-lab@ restart loop
periods.bounded: StartLimitBurst=5 within StartLimitIntervalSec=60, then the unit stays failed
periods.note: Only after a service exits with an error (zla_konfiguracia_sluzby, a crash): RestartSec=3 plus the start of python3, about 3.25 s (KOSTRA B5).

periods.name: nginx access log flush
periods.note: access_log ... buffer=32k flush=2s: nginx writes its buffered access log at least every 2 s while requests arrive (a write, no process; lab/guest_state.py waits for it when a segment is cut).

periods.name: hyptcn-lab-udrzba.timer
periods.note: Maintenance in every profile: python3, psql (VACUUM ANALYZE) and gzip of the document log. OnCalendar every 10 minutes, RandomizedDelaySec=300 drawn anew per run, AccuracySec=1s.

periods.name: worker loop
periods.note: Pause uniform 0.8 to 1.2 s after each round (pending orders completed, heartbeat, retention). A queued report runs inside the round as three subprocesses (psql; bash with sort and gzip; install), at most one at a time.

periods.name: HTTP server poll
periods.note: socketserver serve_forever wakes every poll_interval (0.5 s) in each of auth, catalog, orders and docs.

periods.name: event stop health wait
periods.note: Only in the stop of an event or a control, until /healthz answers 200.

periods.name: control start and stop wait
periods.bounded: START_WAIT_S 10 s at a start; STOP_WAIT_S 10 s, then KILL_WAIT_S 5 s after SIGKILL, at a stop
periods.note: Only in the start and the stop of a control (role test_controls, package B8): until its program reported ready, until no process of its session is left.

periods.name: control memory writer loop
periods.bounded: the stop of its occurrence ends it (SIGTERM to its session); the program ends itself after PROGRAM_MAX_S 3600 s
periods.note: Only during an occurrence of kontrola_zapisovac_pamate (role test_controls, 120 to 360 s): the control rewrites its 16, 64 or 256 MiB with random bytes once per collection interval (5 s, the lead's judgment, skeleton B8 section 1), its negative wrote them once and only reports; one report line per round into its output file.

periods.name: control process batch loop
periods.bounded: the stop of its occurrence ends it (SIGTERM to its session); the program ends itself after PROGRAM_MAX_S 3600 s
periods.note: Only during an occurrence of kontrola_davka_procesov (role test_controls, 120 to 360 s): the control starts a sleep process every 1/K s (K = 2, 10 or 50: 0.5, 0.1 or 0.02 s; period_s is the shortest), each living 2 s (the executor's judgment: at least 4 alive at any instant, none in two snapshots); its negative starts one process for the whole occurrence; one report line a second.

periods.name: log segment reopen wait
periods.note: Only between sessions (segment), until nginx has reopened its logs.

periods.name: deployment health wait
periods.note: Only at deployment: two curl processes per try.

periods.name: PostgreSQL autovacuum launcher
periods.exception: Exception from the first point of proposal 5.6 (a process-creating loop without a bound and without a random delay, outside the lab's code): autovacuum stays on (lead's answer to Q3, 2026-11-22T20:55Z: PostgreSQL's defaults, and this exception); its takt is autovacuum_naptime 67 s (lead's answer to Q9, 2026-11-24: the cause removed at its source, principle 7 and D11), so the spacing of the worker starts lies 1 to 4 s from a multiple of the collection interval, which the lab test and G2 check (scripts/lab_trial.py AUTOVACUUM_REMAINDER_S); campaign v6 accepted 48 of 48 sessions at 60 s. Periodicity of flagged rows stays the main check.
periods.note: One worker process per database every autovacuum_naptime (67 s, lab/hyptcn-lab-postgresql.conf); three databases accept connections (hyptcn_lab, postgres, template1), so one start every 67/3 = 22.333333 s, on a grid fixed by the start of the server; another number of databases changes the spacing, so it is measured. hyptcn-lab-udrzba runs on top of it, it does not replace it.

before.logging: log_min_messages debug1 for that run only (docs/ODCHYLKY_V5.sk.md, entry 4)

measured.pending: Measured in the one window on the VM before the G0 record (lead's answer to Q27): labctl deploy with lab/hyptcn-lab-postgresql.conf, then one run of lab_trial long --postgres-debug1, whose record of stage skuska fills in after here, before the G0 record; the property: the median spacing modulo interval_s lies in [1, 4] s.

periods.name: PostgreSQL checkpointer
periods.note: Writes dirty buffers at least every checkpoint_timeout, earlier when max_wal_size fills.

periods.name: PostgreSQL background and WAL writers
periods.note: Wake every 200 ms; they hibernate longer when there is nothing to write.

periods.name: systemd-journald sync
periods.note: Syncs the journal files to disk; messages of priority crit and above sync at once.

periods.name: kernel writeback
periods.note: Flusher threads wake every 5 s, the collection period; kernel threads, no process created by the writeback.

periods.name: systemd-timesyncd poll
periods.source: system: timesyncd.conf PollIntervalMinSec (default 32 s, growing to PollIntervalMaxSec 2048 s)
periods.note: NTP poll; the interval grows while the clock stays synchronized.
